result.rationale: When credential sharing is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response (from `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...)`), which has no `.data` property. In googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts the new code does `const res = await refreshOAuthTokens(...); const token = res?.data; googleCredentials.access_token = token.access_token;` — with sharing on, `token` is undefined and `token.access_token` throws TypeError on every refresh. The non-shared path returns `fetchTokens.res` (gaxios) which has `.data`, so only the new sharing path is broken.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `refreshAccessToken` now calls `refreshOAuthTokens(...)` and then does `const token = res?.data; googleCredentials.access_token = token.access_token;`. But `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the result of `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...)` when sharing is enabled (see `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`), which is a standard `Response` object that does not have a `.data` property. Therefore `token` becomes `undefined` and `token.access_token` will throw a TypeError during refresh when credential sharing + sync endpoint are enabled.
